Q: Confusion resolving NuGet package vulnerabilities A:

To reproduce :

  • dotnet new classlib
  • dotnet add package MailKit --version 4.15.0

Then to show the vulnerability dotnet package list points to the problematic dependency:

warning NU1902: Package 'MimeKit' 4.15.0 has a known moderate severity vulnerability, https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-g7hc-96xr-gvvx

And dotnet package update fixes it:

Updating MailKit 4.15.0 to 4.15.1.

Q: What is the difference between these mapping libraries A:

To make sense of these options, try to separate them into two groups first, like renderers that draw the map (Leaflet, MapLibre, Mapbox GL JS) and data providers that supply the map imagery and terrain (Mapbox, MapTiler, OpenFreeMap, OpenMapTiles).

Leaflet is a great 2D renderer, but since you are building a tool to "show terrains with a route path", you need a 3D renderer like Mapbox GL JS (paid) or MapLibre (free and open-source). For the data itself, Mapbox and MapTiler both offer excellent 3D terrain and satellite imagery, with recency varying heavily by region for all providers.

Your best bet is to use MapLibre to render the map for free, and plug in 3D terrain data from a provider like MapTiler or Mapbox to draw your routes over it.

Q: How can I save k8s pod logs to host disk A:

You could use liblogtap to intercept the legacy log and to route it to stdout managed by the CRE or to a fluentd daemonset.

See below an excerpt of a example deployment. The library gets injected into the application container using an init container which is writing liblogtap.so to a shared volume from where the application container loads the (LD_PRELOAD).

Meanwhile the sidecar spins up and the logforwarder opens a socket (in the same shared volume) to which the libary inside the legacy app container connects, writing the intercepted logs there. The logforwarder can send the captured logs to stdout, a fluent sink or both.

Benefits: No need to modify application or docker image and reduced disk i/o.

liblogtap is open source and to be found at [github](https://github.com/katalyticIT/liblogtap/tree/main).

      volumes:
      - name: shared-data  # shared volume for library and socket
        emptyDir: {}

      initContainers:
      # 1. The init container which injects the library via the shared volume
      - name: install-tap
        image: katalytic/liblogtap-demo:1.0
        imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
        command: ["cp", "-v", "/usr/local/lib/liblogtap.so", "/var/run/liblogtap.so"]
        volumeMounts:
        - name: shared-data
          mountPath: /var/run

      containers:
      # 2. The main app, writing to a log file
      - name: main-app
        image: your/app-image:tag
        command: ["/path/to/legacyapp"]
        env:
        - name:  LD_PRELOAD
          value: "/var/run/liblogtap.so"
        - name:  LLT_TAP_FILE             # path to legacy log file
          value: "/var/log/app.log
        - name:  LLT_SUPPRESS_TAP_FILE    # don't write to disk
          value: "true"
        - name:  LLT_TARGET               # write to socket
          value: "socket:/var/run/sidecar-logging.sock"
        volumeMounts:
        - name: shared-data
          mountPath: /var/run

      # 3. The Sidecar using an image with a simple go-written log forwarder
      - name: sidecar
        image: katalytic/logfwd:1.0
        env:
        - name:  SOCKET_PATH         # must be the same socket as above
          value: "/var/run/sidecar-logging.sock"
        - name:  SINK_STDOUT         # set to true to let an existing
          value: "false"             # fluentd pick the sidecar logs up
        - name:  SINK_FLUENT         # Maybe faster because reducing disk i/o
          value: "fluentd-receiver-svc:24224"
        volumeMounts:
        - name: shared-data
          mountPath: /var/run

Q: How can I install pygame on Python 3.14? A:

Pygame doesn't support Python 3.14. Support has been requested, but there hasn't been an update to provide it.

If you want pygame and don't care that much about 3.14, downgrading to 3.13 should fix the problem. If you're really ardent about 3.14, maybe consider python-ce; it's a Pygame fork with more frequent updates and has official 3.14 support.
